plugins.name: Web-Safe
plugins.description: The classic web-safe browser palette from the 1990s, built from a 6x6x6 RGB cube for early displays with limited color fidelity.

plugins.name: Green Phosphor
plugins.description: A simple 2-color green-phosphor monitor palette inspired by monochrome CRT displays used on early terminals and PCs.

plugins.name: Amber Phosphor
plugins.description: A simple 2-color amber-phosphor monitor palette inspired by monochrome CRT displays used on early terminals and word processors.

plugins.name: Windows 16
plugins.description: The standard 16-color Windows system palette used by legacy VGA-era software and desktop themes.

plugins.name: ANSI 16
plugins.description: The traditional 16-color ANSI terminal palette, combining 8 base colors with their bright counterparts.

plugins.name: Extended ANSI / Xterm
plugins.description: The 256-color xterm palette: ANSI 16, a 6x6x6 color cube, and a grayscale ramp used by many terminal emulators.

plugins.name: EGA
plugins.description: IBM Enhanced Graphics Adapter 16-color palette, common in late DOS software before VGA became dominant.

plugins.name: Commodore 64
plugins.description: The standard 16-color Commodore 64 palette derived from the VIC-II graphics chip and widely used in C64 artwork and games.

plugins.name: Atari 400
plugins.description: A representative Atari 400/800-era palette based on the machine's CTIA/GTIA color-luminance combinations without artifact color simulation.

plugins.name: Atari 400 Artifacting
plugins.description: An expanded Atari 400/800-inspired palette that includes artifact-style color behavior associated with composite display output.

plugins.name: CGA 0
plugins.description: IBM CGA palette 0, the cyan-magenta-white set commonly seen in early composite and RGBI PC graphics.

plugins.name: CGA 1
plugins.description: IBM CGA palette 1, the green-red-brown set used by many early DOS games and applications.
